scenes.headline: CDC Pipelines
scenes.subtitle: Keep a Delta replica in sync with a source
scenes.narration: Change data capture pipelines apply inserts, updates, and deletes from a source system into Delta tables.

scenes.headline: What CDC handles
items: Captures row-level changes from operational databases
Applies inserts, updates, and deletes incrementally
scenes.narration: CDC streams the individual changes a source database emits. It applies each insert, update, and delete to keep the target current. The result is a fresh, analytics-ready replica without full reloads.

scenes.headline: Applying changes with MERGE
scenes.code:
MERGE INTO silver.products AS t
USING cdc_updates AS s
ON t.product_id = s.product_id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'DELETE' THEN DELETE
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'UPDATE' THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND s.op != 'DELETE' THEN INSERT *;
scenes.narration: MERGE matches incoming change rows against the target on the primary key. Deletes remove rows, updates overwrite them, and new keys are inserted. This upsert pattern keeps the silver replica consistent with the source.

scenes.headline: MERGE vs APPLY CHANGES INTO (DLT)
scenes.narration: A hand-written MERGE gives full control but you must manage event ordering yourself. Delta Live Tables' APPLY CHANGES INTO handles CDC declaratively, reconciling out-of-order events automatically. It even supports slowly changing dimension types one and two out of the box.

scenes.headline: Watch out for
items: Correctly sequencing updates with a version column
Handling hard deletes versus soft deletes
scenes.narration: Change events can arrive late or out of order and must be sequenced. A sequence or version column ensures the newest change wins. Deciding between hard and soft deletes shapes your downstream history.

scenes.text: CDC keeps your lakehouse in lockstep with source systems, one change at a time.
scenes.narration: Incremental upserts beat full reloads for both freshness and cost.
